Copied verbatim into the repo per that document's implementation-order step 6 ("Import the compass profiles as draft, never as verified catalogue records"). Extended with Find_Your_Class_Scoring_Batch_01_Compass_Completion_v1.json (overlay completing the original 7 to 56/56 numeric + 8 categorical) and Find_Your_Class_Scoring_Batches_02-06 (20 additional fully-scored archetype profiles), handed off by Codex as Find_Your_Class_Scoring_ALL_Batches_01-06_100pct.zip.

profiles.editorialNote: The non-magical ranged endurance anchor. Trick Shot gives it more physical disruption than a generic bow damage profile, especially from level 3 onward.
The armour-and-shield survival anchor. Its chassis is exceptionally hard to hurt, but protecting allies still depends heavily on positioning, reach and build choices.
The infiltration and protected-site exploration anchor. Combat impact is conditional rather than weak: it depends on creating sneak-attack opportunities.
The spontaneous full-arcane anchor, assuming a non-companion bloodline. Spell selection is highly consequential, hence high build fragility despite low daily preparation.
The broad prepared nature-toolbox anchor without a persistent animal companion. Summoning remains available, so extra-entity burden is low rather than absent.
The multiple-persistent-companion anchor. Dividing effective druid levels makes companion allocation a consequential and relatively fragile build decision.
The ranged spell-and-weapon burst anchor. Its bonded ranged weapon is equipment dependence, not a creature companion; category wording should eventually separate bonded object from sentient item.

profiles.name: Eldritch Guardian
compassAnchors: The highest companion centrality among the Fighter pilot paths
A martial familiar-sharing anchor rather than a spellcaster
profiles.playerSummary: You remain a full martial combatant, but your familiar becomes a trained partner that can share your combat feats. It adds scouting, utility and a second body to manage without turning you into a spellcaster.
profiles.tradeoff: The familiar opens clever combinations, but costs early bonus feats and makes both building and running the character more demanding.

profiles.name: Lore Warden
profiles.sourceEditionNote: Scored against the Adventurer's Guide version currently shown by Archives of Nethys. Do not mix it with older Lore Warden text.
profiles.playerSummary: You fight by understanding the enemy: knowledge, Combat Expertise and a deep manoeuvre toolkit turn the Fighter into a learned battlefield technician.
profiles.tradeoff: You give up medium armour, heavy armour and shields, and the path rewards a player comfortable with manoeuvre rules and carefully connected feat choices.

profiles.name: Mutation Warrior
profiles.playerSummary: You are still unmistakably a Fighter, but a mutagen lets you become stronger, tougher or more bestial when the important battle arrives.
profiles.tradeoff: Its strongest form is limited by mutagen use and discovery choices, and the physical boost comes with a mental-ability penalty while active.

profiles.name: Charlatan
profiles.playerSummary: You win access, trust and influence by making other people believe the story you need them to hear. In a social or intrigue-heavy campaign, the con itself becomes one of your strongest tools.
profiles.tradeoff: You give up trapfinding and trap sense, so this is not the Rogue to choose if defeating protected mechanisms is central to your idea.

profiles.name: Eldritch Scoundrel

compatibilityGates.rule: Not available for use with the Unchained Rogue.

compassAnchors: A direct bridge between Rogue and Magus without spell combat
profiles.playerSummary: You approach the ruin as both thief and wizard: stealth gets you inside, and a prepared arcane spellbook lets you bypass the obstacle that tools alone cannot solve.
profiles.tradeoff: You lose half the Rogue's skill ranks, most of its sneak-attack progression, armour proficiency and many talents. It is a demanding hybrid, not a normal Rogue with a few bonus spells.

profiles.name: Scout
profiles.playerSummary: You create your own opening by moving: charge through the gap or cross the battlefield, then turn that momentum into sneak-attack damage without waiting for an ally to flank.
profiles.tradeoff: The payoff favours one decisive attack after movement rather than a stationary full attack, and enemies with uncanny dodge can shut down the archetype's signature shortcut.

profiles.name: Thug
profiles.playerSummary: You turn threat into battlefield control: frightened enemies run, and a brutal sneak attack can leave a target sickened instead of dealing every last die of damage.
profiles.tradeoff: You surrender trapfinding and trap sense, and fear tactics lose value against immune enemies.

profiles.name: Crossblooded
profiles.playerSummary: Two bloodlines let you combine powers and arcana that a normal Sorcerer can never hold together, creating an unusually focused magical identity.
profiles.tradeoff: You know one fewer spell at every spell level and take a permanent penalty to Will saves. Weak spell and bloodline choices are exceptionally costly.

profiles.name: Eldritch Scrapper
profiles.playerSummary: You are an innate full caster who can borrow the combat feat needed for the fight in front of you, blending spells with improvised martial technique.
profiles.tradeoff: You still have a Sorcerer's attack progression, hit points and armour limits. Martial flexibility demands deep feat knowledge and replaces several bloodline powers.

profiles.name: Razmiran Priest

changeOrAtonementNotes: The archetype's identity is explicitly that of a missionary servant of Razmir; verify whether the selected campaign treats this narrative identity as a formal prerequisite.

compatibilityGates.rule: Razmiran Channel, the major divine-item access feature, begins at level 9.
Requires divine spell-trigger or spell-completion items to realise its broadest access.

profiles.playerSummary: You are an arcane confidence artist wearing the role of a priest, eventually fuelling divine scrolls and wands with your own sorcerous power.
profiles.tradeoff: The defining trick arrives at level 9 and relies on carrying suitable divine items, making the character expensive, rules-heavy and strongly tied to Razmir's religious institution.

profiles.name: Seeker
profiles.playerSummary: Your bloodline is a mystery to investigate. You bring full Sorcerer magic into forgotten ruins while gaining the rare ability to find and disable magical traps.
profiles.tradeoff: You remain a low-skill-rank Sorcerer, so Intelligence and skill allocation matter if you want to live up to the investigator fantasy.

profiles.name: Tattooed Sorcerer
compassAnchors: The familiar-with-low-management escape hatch: it can become a passive tattoo
profiles.playerSummary: Your magic is written across your body, and your familiar can step out of a living tattoo when you need a companion rather than constant extra management.
profiles.tradeoff: You trade selected bloodline powers and a bloodline feat for tattoo magic, and much of the exact magical role still depends on bloodline and spells known.

profiles.name: Feyspeaker
profiles.playerSummary: You are a fey-touched full nature caster who can speak for the party and weave enchantment and illusion into the Druid's enormous prepared toolbox.
profiles.tradeoff: Your combat ability becomes caster-like: weaker attack progression, no medium armour, delayed Wild Shape and no spontaneous summoning.

profiles.name: Nature Fang
compassAnchors: The full-caster studied-target weapon hunter anchor
profiles.playerSummary: You keep the Druid's full prepared magic but hunt despoilers of nature with Studied Target, Sneak Attack and a growing selection of Slayer talents.
profiles.tradeoff: You give up Wild Shape completely. Fighting well with weapons also pulls your ability scores and build choices in more directions than a caster-first Druid.

profiles.name: Reincarnated Druid
profiles.playerSummary: From 5th level onward, death usually changes your face rather than ending your story. You retain the Druid's huge magical toolbox while embodying nature's cycle of renewal.
profiles.tradeoff: Many Lives waits a full day, fails against death effects and cannot trigger again for seven days. Wild Shape also arrives late and functions two levels behind.

profiles.name: Storm Druid

compatibilityGates.rule: Must choose Air or Weather domain, or Cloud, Storm or Wind subdomain; cannot choose an animal companion.

profiles.playerSummary: You look upward rather than into the forest, turning wind, cloud and violent weather into immediate battlefield presence while converting prepared spells into domain magic on demand.
profiles.tradeoff: Your domain is tightly restricted, you can never choose an animal companion, and giving up spontaneous summoning narrows one of the base Druid's most flexible tools.

profiles.name: Armored Battlemage
profiles.playerSummary: You turn the Magus into an arcane heavy infantryman, enhancing armour instead of a weapon and casting confidently inside steel.
profiles.tradeoff: You lose Spell Combat—the defining attack-and-cast rhythm of the normal Magus—along with several arcana and later improvements.

profiles.name: Bladebound

changeOrAtonementNotes: The blade shares the wielder's alignment but has its own mission and Ego; disagreement can produce intelligent-item dominance conflicts rather than class-feature loss.

compatibilityGates.rule: The black blade must be a one-handed slashing weapon, rapier or sword cane; weapon type cannot later be changed.

profiles.playerSummary: Your signature weapon is a conscious partner with its own voice, powers and hidden purpose. The relationship is as central to the story as Spellstrike is to the fighting style.
profiles.tradeoff: Your weapon choice is permanent, your normal arcane pool is smaller, and the blade's growing Ego can turn disagreement into a real contest of wills.

profiles.name: Eldritch Scion
compassAnchors: The resource-gated early Spell Combat anchor
profiles.playerSummary: Your weapon magic comes from instinct and bloodline rather than study: you cast spontaneously and power bloodline abilities through a personal eldritch pool.
profiles.tradeoff: Your spells known are narrow, your bloodline is permanent, and before 8th level Spell Combat consumes mystical focus, making action and resource management particularly demanding.

profiles.name: Hexcrafter
compassAnchors: The reusable-hex and weapon-delivered curse anchor
profiles.playerSummary: You weave a Witch's hexes and a wider catalogue of curses into the Magus chassis, weakening enemies repeatedly before delivering prepared curses through your weapon.
profiles.tradeoff: Hex and arcana selection creates a dense build, and many effects depend on enemy immunities, saving throws or once-per-target limits.
